image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Straight section of elevated expressway deck viewed from below and the side, a single deep trapezoidal concrete box girder with sloping webs and a flat soffit carrying a wide flat road slab that cantilevers out past the box on both sides, solid concrete parapet walls along both edges, a round drain pipe running along the soffit edge, three lanes of asphalt on top Materials: Pale grey precast concrete soffit with segment joint lines every three metres, black soot and rust drip streaks under the drain pipe, grey asphalt with white dashed lane lines and a yellow edge line on top, grimy parapet with rust weep at the joints.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.91. 310/32,000 triangles, 4/24 draw calls, 4/16 materials, 4/32 unique geometries, three canvases.

featureReviews.evidence: Bounds +-6.25, 0..3.5, +-8 off the built module: the contract exactly. Section from the sweep: 7 m soffit, webs to 9.3 m at 2.05, 12.5 m slab, parapets to 3.50, road at 2.40. End faces vertical planes at z +-8.
Yellow edge lines and two dashed white lane lines at fixed v on the 11.4 m road canvas; joints every 2.67 m on the parapet faces (six segments); kerb kick and parapet chamfers read in the hero.

Probed on beauty-hero: road 137 (plate 117; 115 from the turntable elevation), web 132-141 (128), parapet ~141 (122-149). Soot bands on both upper webs; the pipe with three collars and two brackets under the +X cantilever.
featureReviews.notes: The plate's soot is heavier on the near web; the canvas is symmetric.

name: Expressway Box-Girder Deck Module
nameTh: พื้นสะพานทางด่วนคานกล่อง
notes: The standard span piece; the underside is what the player sees, so the soffit, webs, drain pipe and joint lines are the identity. MODULAR CONTRACT for the highway set: the pivot is the centre of the SOFFIT (the girder's underside), so the module is placed at y=12 to sit on any pier whose bearing seat is at y=12; the deck runs along Z from z=-8 to z=+8 and the next module butts against it there, so the end faces are flat, square and carry no overhang; road surface at pivot+2.40, parapet top at pivot+3.50; slab 12.5 m wide along X, box girder 7 m wide at the soffit. No interior to the box. Never sculpt end-face detail that would z-fight with the neighbour.
